# dsh-ssh-logs
English | Simplified Chinese
Controlled SSH command execution for DeepSeek Harness, with a Web configuration page and `@server` c
omposer selection. After installation, add, edit, or remove servers under Settings > Plugins > SSH s
selection. After installation, add, edit, or remove servers under Settings > Plugins > SSH servers.
## Install
Requires DSH `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` and Node.js 20 or later.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart `dsh web` and refresh the page. The bundle loads the Host configuration service, Web setting
s view, and constrained MCP tools.
## SSH configuration
Each server has:

- A stable SSH name used in conversations
- Host or IP address, port, and username
- Password authen

tication, with legacy YAML SSH-key configuration supported
- `allowedCommands`: the executable names

permitted only in read-write mode (optional for legacy YAML)
- `deniedCommands`: an optional list t
hat always overrides the allowlist
Passwords are stored on the DSH host in `$DSH_HOME/ssh-logs/servers.json` with mode `0600`. Neither
the API nor browser returns passwords; editing with a blank password preserves it only if the connec
tion identity is unchanged. Changing host, port, user, jump host, or identity file requires new cred
ntity is unchanged. Changing host, port, user, jump host, or identity file requires new credentials.
Password authentication cannot be combined with `proxyJump`; use an SSH key for jump-host connection
s. Password authentication runs SSH with `-F /dev/null`, ignoring user and system SSH configuration,
including host aliases, proxy commands, and other custom options. Configure the real host, port, us
er and known-hosts file explicitly. Key-based authentication retains the normal SSH configuration be
known-hosts file explicitly. Key-based authentication retains the normal SSH configuration behavior.
Read-only servers expose `read_log` and `search_log` for roots configured in YAML. General `run_remo
te_command` requires explicitly enabling remote commands (read-write) and a non-empty executable all
owlist. The allowlist is not a sandbox: approved programs and arguments can modify files or execute
other programs. Never enable this for untrusted users or servers.
Legacy configurations without `allowedCommands` remain usable for root-based log tools, but no gener
al commands are allowed. A settings-page server overrides a same-name YAML server; configure log roo
ts in YAML on a separate alias. Log-root checks are lexical and do not prevent remote symlinks from
escaping the root. Enforce read-only access and path restrictions with server-side account permissio
aping the root. Enforce read-only access and path restrictions with server-side account permissions.
## Use in conversations
Type `@` in the composer and select an SSH server:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The picker inserts `@server-name`. Use the root-based log tools for read-only servers; general comma
nds require read-write authorization. Credentials never enter conversation context.
## Security boundaries
- SSH requires a trusted host key in `known_hosts`. Verify the fingerprint through an independent ch

annel before adding it; `ssh-keyscan` alone does not authenticate a host.
- Commands are default-den

y and a denial always overrides an allow rule.
- Each request is one command: shell control operator

s, pipes, redirects, substitutions, and line breaks are rejected.
- Command output has byte and time

out limits.
- Passwords are never returned through the API, MCP server list, or `@` candidates.
- Pr
oduction deployments should still use dedicated low-privilege accounts, source-IP restrictions, and
server-side permissions.
